Lord Grey Academy is a diverse and vibrant learning community where students develop skills in, and beyond, the classroom to ensure they flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: Home & School Partnership - Lord Grey Academy
pageCache.text:
At Lord Grey Academy, we are committed to giving every student the best possible opportunity to learn, grow, and thrive—both academically and personally. We believe that a strong, positive partnership between home, students, and the Academy is essential to achieving this goal.
To support this shared mission, we have outlined the key responsibilities that each member of our community—students, parents/carers, and staff—should uphold as part of this important partnership.
STUDENT RESPONSIBILITIES
Follow the Lord Grey Way at all times Bring the correct equipment so you can fully take part in your lessons Keep your phone/electronic devices in your bag, turned off, from arrival through the school entrance until you leave school at 3.15 so that your learning, and that of others, is disruption free. Complete Self-Study each week by the deadline set. Follow the Climates for Learning to help you and your class learn. Wear your full uniform, including PE kit, correctly and with pride every day. Uphold our school values and behaviour guidelines at all times including on the way to and from school. Keep our school environment clean, tidy and damage free. Engage positively with any sanctions or support to modify your conduct. E.g. detentions. Communicate with staff in a polite, courteous and respectful manner to enable concerns and queries to be effectively resolved.
PARENT RESPONSIBILITIES
Ensure your child attends punctually and properly equipped each day. Please inform the academy each day of any absences should they be unwell or cannot attend. Encourage and support your child’s learning by ensuring all Self-Study tasks are completed and submitted on time. Ensure your child is wearing the school uniform as described in the Academy’s Uniform Policy. Understand and actively support the Academy’s policies and guidelines for behaviour, encouraging children to take responsibility for their actions and support the school – the Lord Grey Way. Support your child by attending Parents’ Evenings and engagement events, whether in person or virtually. Encourage your child to read widely at home. Support your child in using social media safely and responsibly, having regular conversations about their online footprint. Regularly use the MCAS app to stay informed and engage in meaningful conversations with your child. Contact Health, Welfare and Reception to relay messages to your child, please do not call or message your child during the school day. Communicate with staff in a polite, courteous and respectful manner to enable concerns and queries to be effectively resolved.
ACADEMY RESPONSIBILITIES
Provide a safe and supportive environment for all students. Uphold high standards and expectations for student achievement and behaviour by following the Lord Grey Way. Work collaboratively with students to maximise their progress in lessons. Recognise and reward students who show our character values and get things right. Offer useful feedback, and provide opportunities for students to enact feedback, in order for students to help accelerate their learning. Communicate regularly with parents and students to keep them well informed about Academy events. Keep parents/carers updated on their child’s progress through the MCAS app. Communicate with students and parents/carers in a polite, courteous and respectful manner, to enable concerns and queries to be effectively resolved. We aim to respond to parent/carers’ emails and phone calls within 48 hours where practicable. Offer school trips, visits, events and year groups events as privileges that support student growth and reserve the right to remove the privilege should we need to.
Together, we build a strong, caring community where every student can succeed. Thank you for being part of our shared journey.

Partner With Us: Help Shape Future Careers
At Lord Grey Academy, we are passionate about connecting our students with the world of work. We want to give every student the best possible start to their career journey, and we cannot do this without the support of our community.
We would love to hear from
How You Can Get Involved If you, your business, or your training centre can support our students, here are some of the ways you can help:
Inspire Our Students: Local Business Partnerships Wanted
At Lord Grey Academy, we are committed to providing our students with a comprehensive understanding of the professional world. To achieve this, we are looking to bridge the gap between the classroom and the workplace—and we need your help.
Share Your Expertise
Do you work for or own a local business? Your experience is one of the most valuable resources our students can access. We are looking for professionals from all sectors to provide our students with genuine insight into different career paths, industry trends, and the “working world.”
By sharing your journey, you can help spark a passion in a young person and help them make informed decisions about their future.
How to Get Involved
Whether it’s through a guest talk, a workplace visit, or a Q&A session, we would love to hear how you might be able to contribute to our careers programme.
If you are interested in supporting the next generation of professionals, please register your interest via the link below:
Click here to complete our Business Interest Form
Thank you for your continued support of Lord Grey Academy and our students’ professional development.
Get in Touch If you are able to support any of these activities or have other opportunities to offer, please contact our team:
You can find further details on our main Careers and Futures Guidance page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome 2026 Year 6 Parents & Carers - Lord Grey Academy
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Your Future: Joining the Class of 2026
Welcome to Lord Grey Academy! We are absolutely delighted that you will be joining our vibrant school community this coming September 2026.
The transition from primary to secondary school is one of life’s great milestones. It’s a time of new friendships, new subjects, and new opportunities to discover exactly who you want to be.
At Lord Grey Academy, we pride ourselves on being a supportive “collaboration between home and school” where every student is encouraged to strive for high standards and live out our core values.
Our motto, ‘Lord Grey Can’ reminds all members of our community that there is no limit to our ambition where imagination can become reality. Our Aim is to provide a stimulating learning environment, a broad curriculum and the highest quality pastoral care so that all our students flourish.
Our values of Determination, Ambition, Curiosity, Integrity and Civility are caught, taught and sought out so that we develop the character of Lord Grey students to prepare them for life beyond school
What to Expect This Summer
We know you might be feeling a mix of excitement and a few “first-day jitters”—that’s completely normal! To make sure you feel like a part of the family before you even step through the doors, we have a full transition program planned:
Transition Days: Come and experience a “day in the life” of a Lord Grey student.
Meet Your Tutors: Get to know the teachers who will be your mentors throughout your journey.
Parent Information Evening: Ensuring the whole family feels prepared for the leap to Year 7.
Our Promise to You
At Lord Grey, we live by the motto: “Lord Grey Can.” Whether you are an aspiring scientist, a talented athlete, a creative artist, or a future leader, we are here to provide the platform for your success.
“The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. We can’t wait to take those first steps with you this September.”
We look forward to meeting you all very soon!
Frequently Asked Questions: Transitioning to Year 7
Moving to secondary school brings up a lot of practical questions. Here are the answers to the things our new families ask most often:
When is the first day?
Term starts in early September 2026. You will receive a specific induction date in your welcome pack later this spring.
What is the school uniform?
Our uniform consists of the Lord Grey blazer, tie, and option of branded PE kit or plain black. A full list of approved suppliers and “Frequently Asked” uniform tips is available in our [Uniform Guide].
From September 2026 when the new term starts, we will be introducing Phone Pouches for all of our students which will ‘live’ with your student from Year 7 up until they finish their Journey with Lord Grey Academy.
How are ‘Sets’ decided?
We use a combination of SATs results, primary school teacher recommendations, and our own internal assessments to ensure students are in the best environment for their pace of learning. On entry, for the first four weeks, we do some transition work on Literacy, Numeracy and take a deep look at work set from the October Half Term.
What if my child gets lost?
Don’t worry! The school is large, but for the first week, Year 7s have plenty of support and student buddies to help them find their way between classrooms. Their first day is the first day of school with Year 12s. The remaining years follow the following day.
School transport information
Home to School Transport Information
Key Contact Points
If you have a specific query regarding your child’s transition, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our dedicated transition team:
Admissions Queries: admissions@lordgrey.org.uk
SEND Support: sendadmin@lordgrey.org.uk
General Office: 01908 626110
Pro Tip for Students: Start practising your new morning routine and “packing your bag” a week before school starts. It makes the first morning much more relaxed!
Your “Ready for Greatness” Summer Checklist
We want you to arrive in September feeling confident and prepared. Here is a handy checklist for you to tick off as you enjoy your summer break!

Dear Parents, Carers and Guardians,
We are delighted that your child has been offered a place at Lord Grey Academy and will join us as a Year 7 student in September 2026.
You can find a copy of your welcome letter from me, Mrs Satyanadhan, here.
If you have not as yet received a paper copy of the Enrolment form, Medical form and Communication consent form which were posted to you or if for whatever reason you have misplaced them and require a new copy, please feel free to download and print a copy here: Starter pack, Enrolment, Medical and Communication consent form.
Please do not send any of these forms via email as we require the paper copies to be returned to us.
I am sure that your child will be excited about joining Lord Grey but i expect that there may be some nervousness as well and i know that parents will be anxious about the transition to secondary school too. Don’t worry, this is all perfectly normal!
We have an exciting and thorough transition programme planned which will help make starting at secondary school a smooth process so that your child settles quickly and thrives in their new school environment.
The behaviour and attitudes of our students is very positive and we are proud of our students and the kind and caring attitudes to each other that they display. This ensures an environment in which learning is good and better for everyone.
We are relentless in our pursuit of excellence with a focus on academic rigour with compassion. We insist on outstanding behaviour within a harmonious and respectful culture, where students feel happy and safe. We encourage our students to become confident and ambitious young adults, balanced by compassion and respect for others.
We ensure that every student has access to an outstanding education and is given the best life opportunities. We create a positive atmosphere, an “I can achieve anything” attitude through our core values and motto, Lord Grey Can!
For more information on our Policies, please click here.
Samantha Satyanadhan Principal

Get a taste of Lord Grey Academy and what we can offer by downloading our main school and Sixth Form prospectus.
We truly believe that Lord Grey CAN. You will find no better staff than the ones at Lord Grey who have dedicated themselves to the young people of our academy and Bletchley.

Our motto, Lord Grey Can reminds all members of our community that there is no limit to our ambition where imagination can become reality. Our Aim is to provide a stimulating learning environment, a broad curriculum and the highest quality pastoral care so that all our students flourish.
We have our community at the heart of what we do.
Mrs Samantha Satyanadhan, Principal

Admissions
Lord Grey Academy Admission Criteria can be viewed and downloaded on the right hand side of the page. It explains all you need to know about admissions to the school at Year 7 and at 16+.
We work closely with the Local Authority admissions team for Year 7 admissions. We adhere to the national Admissions Code.
Mid year admissions Lord Grey’s Admissions Authority is Tove Learning Trust and should you wish to apply for a place at Lord Grey Academy, you are kindly requested to click here or contact our Registrar for advice email registrar@lordgrey.org.uk

Sixth Form applications Applications are made directly to the school. Please see our Sixth Form page for details and application form or contact the Head of Sixth Form, Mr Jason Darvall for information. Email: sixthform@lordgrey.org.uk
Learning for your son/daughter is a three way partnership: learner, parents and teachers. Research shows that good communication between home and school builds trust and success for our students.
Transfer to Secondary School September 2026
Admission arrangements for entry to the Academy in September 2026 can be viewed by downloading the Admissions Criteria 2026-2027 on the right hand side of this page.
When requesting for an Appeal Pack, parents should note that most appeals fail because the schools are already full and do not have the resources to admit additional children without harming the education of the existing pupils.
So please think carefully before making your appeal. They are time-consuming and stressful for parents and expensive for schools (a minimum of £495 plus VAT per appeal held paid by the Academy which is a public funded organisation).
You are unlikely to be successful where you:
Applicants may only apply to the Academy once for each academic year. Applicants who pursue their application to an independent appeal and are then unsuccessful at independent appeal, may not reapply until the following academic year unless there has been a material change of circumstance. These applicants will then not be considered to be in the application process unless they write to The Academy asking to be retained on the waiting list. Therefore, you cannot make a second appeal for the same school for the academic year.
Appeals for Admission to Lord Grey Academy
If you wish to appeal against the non-allocation of a place at Lord Grey Academy, you should contact the Academy directly (the Registrar) to ask for an appeal pack by using the email address registrar@lordgrey.org.uk by the relevant deadline date. Please provide your child’s full name and date of birth when emailing.
THERE ARE IMPORTANT TIME LIMITS FOR MAKING YOUR APPEAL
For Secondary appeals for Year 7, September 2026 entry, if you are refused a school place on 2 March 2026 your appeal form for Lord Grey Academy must be received by the Registrar by 12 noon on 31 March 2026.
We will do our best to ensure appeals submitted by 31 March 2026 are heard by the end of the summer term but regret that some appeals may be delayed due to panel availability.
Appeals made after this date will be heard from September 2026.
For all other appeals, your appeal form should be received by the Registrar at Lord Grey Academy within 28 calendar days of the date you were refused the school place. The appeal will be heard within 40 school days of the deadline for lodging appeals.

Life Beyond the Classroom at Lord Grey Academy
At Lord Grey Academy, education goes far beyond the classroom. Our wide range of extracurricular activities offers students the opportunity to explore their interests, develop new skills, and build lasting friendships. From sports teams and creative arts to academic clubs and leadership opportunities, there’s something for everyone.
We believe these experiences play a vital role in shaping confident, well-rounded individuals who are ready to thrive in all areas of life.

Curriculum Explained
At Lord Grey Academy we pride ourselves on delivering a high quality, high support/ high challenge curriculum that is wholly inclusive to meet the needs of all our learners, with particular regard for students with SEND or disadvantage. We never view our curriculum as a “finished” model, regularly reviewing in light of research-informed evidence, our context and students’ needs. Consequently, our students experience a curriculum that is:
At Lord Grey we have a three year KS3 and a two year KS4, with students making their Guided Choices in Spring Term 2 ready for Year 10.
As we are a large Academy we are able to offer a wide range of subjects which harness everyone’s talents and aptitudes, a breakdown of how we offer this to each student can be found here; Lord Grey Curriculum Model 2025-2026
At Key Stage 3, Lord Grey Students study the following subjects:
English, Maths, Science, History, Geography, RE, PSHE, a Modern Foreign Language of their choice, PE, Music, Drama, Art, and a rotation of Food Technology, Design Technology and CAD/CAM design.
At Key Stage 4, our students are given the opportunity to specialise whilst maintaining breadth. All students study the core subjects of English Language, English Literature, Maths and Combined Science with the opportunity to take Triple Science. All students study PSHRE (which is a combination of PSHE and RE) and Core PE. We block our subjects to ensure students can access the EBACC and all students choose between History, Geography and a Modern Foreign Language with the opportunity to study all 3. There are a range of additional choices available including the following:
Art, Art Photography, Business Studies, Child Development, Computer Science, Design Technology, Drama, Food Technology, Health and Social Care, Hospitality and Catering, IT, Music, Psychology and Sports Science.
The Modern Foreign Languages we offer are German, Italian and Spanish.
Our inclusive sixth form offers a wide range of qualifications, ensuring that the needs of all learners are catered for. We offer a range of A Level and highly successful Level 3 Vocational courses such as Criminology, Business and Applied Science and Applied Psychology. We are one of the only schools in Milton Keynes to offer Level 2 qualification pathway with our Public Services and English and/or Maths resit, should these be required, ensuring there is a place for everyone.
We have an exciting array of enrichment activities on offer that all students select from; these include working with PSG, the EPQ, and the Sports’ leaders programme. All students develop their character and personal skills with a weekly personal development lesson and an extensive programme of additional opportunities to learn about future careers and study options is offered throughout students’ time with us. Our sixth form students also contribute positively to both our school community and the local community through their leadership of the School Council including charity events, mentoring students in the years below and as sports leaders in primary schools.
Note: Parents/Carers have the right to withdraw their child from the non-statutory components of sex education within the RSE programme. The process for requests for withdrawal can be found in Appendix 3 of our RSE Policy which can be found here https://www.lordgrey.org.uk/policies/
Parents/Carers also have the right to withdraw their child from Religious Education and trips and visits of a religious nature. To request the withdrawal of your child from either of the above subjects, please use the form at the link here.

Extra curricular opportunities include participating in the annual school show, school band and choir, languages film club, debating club, the UKMT Maths challenge and a variety of sporting opportunities including UV sports, Cricket and Badminton. Medication and Absence Procedures at Lord Grey Academy
At Lord Grey Academy, student health and safety is a top priority.
Our qualified First Aiders are available to provide immediate care for any accidents, injuries, or medical emergencies that occur during the school day.
The School Health and Welfare Officer manages first aid services, ensuring students receive prompt and appropriate treatment. We are equipped with essential medical supplies, including spare epi-pens and inhalers, to handle urgent situations.
For more serious cases, parents will be contacted, and further medical assistance will be arranged as needed.
Administering Medicines
If students require medication please can we ask that you administer this medication before and after school. If students must have medication during the school day, then this must be prescribed by the GP, in its original packaging to show the dose to be taken daily and clearly marked with the student’s name, DOB and stored with the student services team in the locked medicine cabinet.
Students are NOT allowed to carry medication of any sort on their person, except inhalers, EpiPens and insulin for diabetics.
It is the parents /carers responsibility to ensure that all medication is in date and in a labelled box left with the student services team.
Students are able to seek assistance from the health advisor at break and lunch time, they will be encouraged to wait their turn unless it is an emergency or they are visibly unwell.
Benedict’s Law – Anaphylaxis
The school staff have been trained in the administration of adrenaline devices and the school’s protocol to provide swift and decisive action to any student or staff member who is presenting with an allergic reaction.
The school’s Policy can be found in the Policy section and the poster can be found here to remind staff and students of the protocol at school.
Parents are to provide an email/copy of a medical proof confirming why a pupil requires this. Temporary toilet passes can be given for a short period of time.
If your child has previously required a Medical pass for a confirmed condition, this will be renewed.
Reporting Absence:
Please notify the school by 8:00 am on the first day of absence by calling the absence line at 01908 626167 or emailing attendance.officers@lordgrey.org.uk, providing the student’s name, form group, and reason for absence. This needs to be repeated for each day of absence.
Please notify the school in advance for medical or dental appointments. Whenever possible, please schedule these outside school hours.
For further information, please email: attendance.officers@lordgrey.org.uk.

Careers and Futures Guidance
Our VisionStudents leave Lord Grey with confidence in their skills, abilities and with the tools and knowledge needed to forge successful and fulfilling careers.
At Lord Grey Academy, we believe that Lord Grey Can. We are committed to the idea that our students can achieve anything they set their sights on. We provide a wide range of opportunities to help students discover what they enjoy and where they can excel.
By working with universities, apprenticeship providers, local colleges and employers, we encourage students to aim high. We offer expert advice on UCAS, apprenticeships and vocational courses and further and higher education finance to our students to ensure they are fully prepared for their next steps.
Support for StudentsThe Careers Department provides a variety of resources and support to help all students from Year 7 to Year 13 plan their futures:
Measuring Our ImpactTo ensure we provide the best support, we regularly review our programme through:
Meet the TeamOur careers department consists of a Strategic Lead, Careers Officer and Careers Administrator. Collectively, they provide a range of support, including one-to-one careers guidance, guest speakers, workplace visits and careers events. With their support, our students can explore different career pathways, including college education, apprenticeships, sixth form and university places, as well as gain insights into the qualifications and skills required for their chosen careers.
Haidee Foy: Strategic Lead for Careers & Karen Malone: Level 7 Careers LeadMrs Foy oversees the careers strategy, ensuring the school meets, and exceeds, national standards (Gatsby Benchmarks). Mrs Foy focuses on embedding career education into every school subject.

He also keeps track of each student’s career journey to ensure that every young person has the opportunity to plan confidently for their future beyond school.
A week of formal Work Experience is arranged by students in Year 10 allowing them to experience the process of seeking an employment opportunity, applying and securing a role and then working in a real life setting for a week. Students reflect on their progress and achievement each day and build a portfolio detailing their experience, useful for future employment opportunities.
Students in Year 12 also experience the world of work and we aim to secure 5 days of experience throughout the year with students often securing their own placements in fields that particularly interest them.

Student Leadership
At Lord Grey Academy we believe that every student has the ability to become a leader. Every student should aspire to lead and thus achieve their very best by showing their capabilities and dedication. Leadership is not always easy; it takes strength of character. We encourage our students to gradually develop this inner strength and confidence during their time with us.
There are many different forms of leadership, both at the school and in one’s wider life. A leader is not necessarily someone in charge of an organisation, and nor does a leader need to have many followers. Everyone should lead. Leadership means striving to be the best one can be and setting a good example to others.
Students in the Lower School should be developing their leadership skills. Being able to demonstrate effective leadership skills will benefit our students hugely later in life, as such skills are very attractive to employers. Experience of leading breeds confidence and builds effective communication and listening skills. Students in the Upper School should be leading by being excellent role models, by showing their dedication to academic achievement and by using their own initiative and developing resilience. It is therefore our mission to provide a wealth of leadership opportunities to our students throughout their schooling, and to encourage all students to take up these opportunities.

Uniform, Appearance and Equipment
The Governors and staff at Lord Grey Academy believe that the wearing of a distinctive school uniform makes an important contribution to the tone and reputation of the Academy. It gives students a sense of belonging, and stops students coming to school in clothes which are unsuitable for school.
Maisies Superstore and Kedaph Schoolwear Ltd are the main suppliers of Lord Grey Academy logoed uniform who maintain the agreed standard. The rest of the uniform can be purchased from any high street store or supermarket chain.
Please click here for a downloable version of the Uniform policy.
Sixth Form Uniform
Sixth Form students do not wear uniform, but appearance is important and are expected to wear appropriate clothes for school which is based on the concept of smart office wear. Students on the PSG pathway can wear their PSG clothing. Items can be purchased in the club web shop PSG Academy UK (clubwebshop.com) . We want our Sixth Form students to be treated as individuals and act independently but we also want a collective presence around the school site which younger students, staff and visitors can respect. The many visitors to the Sixth Form judge the students and institution partly on appearances. Looking more professional also translates into taking oneself seriously as a student.
Year 7-11 Uniform

From September 2024 tie colours allocated for their duration at Lord Grey: Year 7 Silver, Year 8- Green, Year 9- Red, Year 10- Yellow Year 11 blue.
**Definition of loose at the ankle – when the student is standing still and upright, the trouser fabric hangs naturally with at least 1.5cm gap between the trouser and the sock for the full circumference of the trouser leg. Thus there is room, hypothetically, to place a finger between the trouser and the sock, without having to stretch the fabric or pull at the seam. A boot cut style is deemed appropriate.

NOTE – If students are unable to take part in PE lessons due to illness or injury your PE kit is still required as you will be involved in the lesson as a coach or ‘teacher’. This will enable you to learn and progress without inhibiting your recovery.
Additional Rules
At Lord Grey Academy we recognise that young people will wish to express their personality through their clothing, wearing of jewellery, and choice of hairstyles. We have a uniform that is worn with pride and we require our students to wear their uniform correctly at all times. We also have some rules that cover jewellery, accessories, hairstyles and other items of clothing that may be worn to school. These rules are kept to a minimum for the sake of clarity and are as follows:
Hair
Long hair must be tied back in practical lessons where long hair could be a danger. Some subjects will have specific rules that all students must follow.
Make-up and nails
Make-up must be discrete and appropriate for school. Students may wear nail polish but false nails, stick on nails and acrylic nails are not permitted for safety and practical reasons
Jewellery
Jewellery should be kept to a minimum and it is essential that high value items should not be worn to school due to the risk of them getting lost. All jewellery should be studs only. Facial piercings other than a stud in the nostril should not be seen. For safety reasons hooped earrings or hooped nose piercings are not allowed in school. All jewellery must be removed for PE lessons including earrings and nose studs. In some practical lessons students will be required to remove jewellery for safety reasons.
Coats and winter wear
We encourage students to wear a coat as each day they spend at least an hour outside in the fresh air. We do not stipulate a type of coat but when worn it should be worn over the blazer and not instead of it or under it. Students may well need to wear a hat, scarf and gloves but these should be removed when in the building.
Hoodies should not be worn as a substitute for a coat.
At Lord Grey Academy we believe that wearing a school uniform provides the students with a sense of belonging and pride in their school. Our uniform expectations are clear in the above information. Uniform Infringements will be sanctioned in accordance with the behaviour policy.
School bag and equipment
Every student must carry a school bag that is suitable to carry everything you need for school. The bag must be big enough to carry a number of A4 sized books/folders. Students should carry in their bag the following items:
Their Knowledge Organiser
Maths Calculator.
